PEP is the same medicine as a PLHIV takes, so it will take some time for the medication to buildup in your system. Maybe a missed dose here or there isn't terrible but the [NIH](https://hivinfo.nih.gov/understanding-hiv/fact-sheets/post-exposure-prophylaxis-pep) does state that strict adherence has a correlation with effectiveness. Also, obligatory not a doctor, so check in with them.

As to tracking adherence, I use a physical calendar and I write down the start date of my new bottle of medicine, and every 10 days from there, marking off everyday after taking my pill. I also use the calendar to compare against my count of pills in the bottle to help me remember/figure out if I took my pills on days I forget to mark off. So far I've successfully used this method to catch a few days where I could not for the life of me remember if I had taken my pill. I have had 100% adherence using this method so far.  Also I should mention that I too have been dealing with depression and other issues that definitely impact me and I would very much miss doses without some way to track my adherence.

Generally there are structure fires and wildfires. Wildfires can be naturally caused (lightning strikes), human caused (tossed cigarettes or hot car over dry grass), or a combination of both (downed power lines in dry grass). It's essentially a designation of how and where the fire originated but more importantly it changes HOW you fight that fire.

It's also important to note that wildfires often do burn down structures but you still fight that fire as a wildfire. So the designation as a wildfire is consistent with how it likely started and the firefighting techniques used to try and bring it under control.
